The route-triggered sink getIdFromSolutionId() was introduced in 2018 (ca9aa136e, pre-AI, human) - it lacks a permission filter by design; the second, separately-called-out sink is the unconditional fallback in getFaqBySolutionId() that re-queries faqdata WITHOUT the permission filter whenever the filtered query returns zero rows. That fallback was first written in 66926d6b4 (2025-10-12, a Mago-formatting commit that also carried this new logic); I verified the fallback is absent from the immediate parent e1a3c2313, that 66926d6b4 is a single-parent (non-squash) commit, and that -S/-G history has no finer public member introducing the same lines, so it is the atomic BIC for the newly-introduced vulnerable fallback. The affected/fixed boundary is exact: 4.1.1 contains 66926d6b4 (vulnerable) and lacks the fix; 4.1.2 contains fix 4e31e12a9 and the fallback is gone - matching advisory vulnerable <=4.1.1 / first_patched 4.1.2. The direct fix hunk removes the fallback and also hardens getIdFromSolutionId. AI second: the BIC commit object carries no AI trailer of any kind - author/committer Thorsten Rinne, message 'refactor: switched code formatting to Mago', empty trailers. Bundle prior hits carry a Co-Authored-By on a different mechanism (PostgreSQL ILIKE) and are not causal for this case. Note: 8551bbe03 (2026-05-02, divergent branch) independently reworked the fallback into a hasRestriction-gated version and is a later parallel fix, not the BIC.
